title: Phased Commitment Proposal — GPU Buffering & Autoscale Margins
body:
Executive summary:

This is a working proposal for a phased capacity commitment with explicit GPU buffering (warm headroom) and autoscale margins for a medium-to-large enterprise POC ("Customer Alpha"). The aim is to propose a commitment curve that reduces unit cost while keeping p95/p99 latency SLAs intact during traffic surges and onboarding fuzziness. Document is intentionally rough — contains assumptions, quick math, and open questions for the workshop on 2026-03-10.

Customer context and ask:
- Customer Alpha expects to launch a conversational assistant integrated into web and mobile. They expect 200k monthly active users in first 6 months, with peak concurrency patterns resembling business-hours spikes concentrated in 3x daily windows.
- Security requirement: Dedicated pool (no multi-tenant mixing) with VPC peering for SSO and audit logs.
- Primary models: 25b open transformer (baseline) and 70b q8f16 variant for high-quality responses.
- SLA ask: p95 < 400ms token-latency for short-turn responses (<=128 tokens); p99 < 700ms.

Workload assumptions (rough):
- Baseline RPS (steady-state): 25 requests/sec (average across full day).
- Peak burst RPS: 200 requests/sec for 10-minute windows during heavy usage; 60 requests/sec sustained for 2 hours during daily peak.
- Average response length: 80 tokens; heavy conversations up to 512 tokens but rare (~2% of requests).
- Average model latency on H100 80GB (optimized runtime, q8f16): ~12ms/token; on A100 80GB: ~18ms/token; small model (25b) ~6ms/token.
- KV cache hit expected for followup prompt patterns: 40% effective cache hit (reduces token compute for followups by ~60%).

Primary goals for sizing and policy:
1) Minimize monthly spend with a commit curve that transitions from low-commit (pilot) to higher-commit (production) in 3 phases over 4 months.
2) Maintain latency SLOs during 99th percentile spikes using a mix of prewarmed buffer GPUs + autoscale burst capacity.
3) Provide fallback model routing (to smaller quantized variants) when burst capacity is exhausted.

Suggested GPU mix and rationale:
- Warm pool (buffer): 2 x H100-80GB (reserved) — handle low-latency p95 traffic and cache-resident workloads. Keeps hot KV caches local and reduces cold-start penalties.
- Core committed pool (phase 2): 4 x H100-80GB (reserved) — supports steady throughput and amortizes cost.
- Burst (on-demand): up to 6 x A10/H100 spot-equivalent or Dedicated burst nodes depending on enterprise preference. Use cheaper GPU types for non-latency-critical batched jobs.
- Fall-through: 3 x 25b quantized (dedicated or pinned) for degraded quality fallback when tail latency risk is high.

Autoscaling policy (proposal):
- Min pool size: 2 H100 (warm pool always online).
- Commit pool (Phase 1): 1 H100 + 1 25b node (pilot).
- Phase 2 commit: 4 H100 (steady state).
- Max pool size with burst: 10 GPUs (combined committed + burst).
- Scale up triggers: sustained queue depth > 0.8 for 30s OR p95 latency breach for 60s.
- Scale down triggers: sustained utilization < 45% for 5 minutes AND no queue backlog.
- Warm headroom: maintain 15-20% spare capacity (based on token throughput distribution) to reduce p99 spikes.
- Prewarm policy: when predicted traffic delta > 30% in next 10 minutes (from scheduled events or forecast), prewarm additional GPU(s) into warm pool immediately to avoid cold scaling delays.

Cost estimates (quick back-of-envelope):
(Assumptions: H100 effective hourly cost to Redwood after cloud discounts = $7/hr equivalent per card when reserved; A100 = $5/hr reserved; burst spot = $1.8/hr avg.)
- Warm pool (2 H100 reserved): 2 * $7 * 24 * 30 = $10,080/mo
- Core committed (4 H100 reserved): 4 * $7 * 24 * 30 = $20,160/mo
- Burst (assume 200h/month averaged across spot usage): 6 * $1.8 * 200 = $2,160/mo (note: this is variable)
- Fallback 25b nodes (3 units at $2.5/hr reserved): 3 * $2.5 * 24 * 30 = $5,400/mo
- Total approximate monthly infra cost = $37.8k/mo (rounded)

Unit economics / per-token cost (very rough):
- Monthly tokens estimate: 200k MAU * avg 150 tokens/session * 2 sessions/user/month = 60M tokens/month. (This is a coarse upper bound.)
- Infrastructure cost per 1k tokens = ($37,800 / 60,000k) * 1000 = $0.63 per 1k tokens (infra-only).
- Notes: this ignores networking, storage, infra overhead, and Redwood platform markup. Also caching improves effective tokens computed — if cache saves 20% of token compute, unit cost drops proportionally.

Risk, mitigations and open questions:
- Cold-start risk for large models: mitigation: keep minimal warm pool of H100s pinned to most-used model variants; increase prewarm window for scheduled spikes.
- Spot instability for burst: mitigation: policy to fallback to smaller quantized local models and queue/retry logic; prefer dedicated burst for regulated customers.
- Cost blowout if traffic > forecast: mitigation: enforce hard routing budget with rate limiting at API gateway and graceful degradation to cheaper model variants.
- Latency regression during long-context requests (>=512 tokens): mitigation: route these to specialized long-context instances with larger batch size and different SLOs.
- Open question: does Customer Alpha accept temporary quality degradation when falling back to 25b? Need to confirm via contract/UX decision. (See JIRA-4321)

Operational runbook notes (short):
- Day 0: provision 2 warm H100 nodes + 1 pilot 25b node, configure autoscale policies, integrate with customer's VPC.
- Day 1–7: collect telemetry, export p50/p95/p99 token latency histograms, validate KV cache hit ratio. Update forecast.
- Scaling incident playbook: on sustained p99 breach > 10 minutes, trigger escalation to SRE + Solutions Eng, prewarm additional H100s immediately and divert new sessions to fallback model.
- Cost control: enable soft caps with email alerts at 60/80/95% of burst budget. Hard caps enforced at 100%.

Workshop agenda items (2026-03-10):
- Walkthrough of assumptions and telemetry we'll collect during pilot.
- Align on acceptable quality fallbacks and UX messaging when degraded.
- Confirm commitment phasing (Milestones: Pilot month -> Ramp month -> Production commit month) and contractual SLA triggers.
- Review monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds.

Open action items (owners):
- Priya: finalize revised hourly cost numbers with finance and put final figures into proposal (ticket: JIRA-4332).
- Ethan: prototype prewarm scheduler that hooks into customer calendar/events (PR #278).
- Maya: prepare sample alert thresholds and dashboard mockups for the console (dashboard ticket).
- Liam: run stress sim with 3x daily peaks using trace replay and produce 95/99 latency curves (sandbox run id pending).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Consider hybrid approach: small fraction of requests (10%) routed to cheaper quantized A100 instances proactively — reduces cost and keeps user experience for majority intact.
- Revisit cache strategy: investigate prefix-level caching for multi-turn flows — could yield >35% token savings in some conversational patterns.
- Re-evaluate GPU pricing assumptions with procurement (H100 $/hr could vary by 15-25% depending on reserved term).
References and links:
- Customer contract draft: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Telemetry spec: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/specs/alpha-pilot
- Scaling sim tool: github.com/redwood-inference/sim-load

This doc is a working draft. Expect numbers to shift after workshop and finance review. Put comments inline in Drive; we'll iterate before sending formal proposal to Customer Alpha."
